prompt: A shop groups customers by buying habits without deciding the groups in advance.
tells: without deciding the groups in advance
why: Nobody decides the groups beforehand; the shop lets buying habits reveal them. Finding groups without labels is clustering.
trap: Classification needs the groups named first.

prompt: Find natural groups of news articles that have no labels.
why: The articles have no labels, and the aim is to find groups that occur naturally. Grouping unlabeled data by similarity is clustering.
trap: With no labels there's nothing to classify into.

prompt: Group songs that sound alike, then name the groups afterward.
why: Songs are grouped first by how they sound, and names come afterward. Discovering groups before naming them is clustering.
trap: Naming after the fact means the groups weren't predefined.

prompt: A biologist sorts cell samples into groups the data suggests, not into known types.
why: The biologist lets the data suggest the groups instead of sorting into known types. Grouping by similarity without known labels is clustering.

prompt: The team wants to discover segments among app users that nobody has defined yet.
why: Nobody has defined the segments yet; the goal is to discover them. Finding groups in unlabeled data is clustering.
trap: Undefined groups can't be classification labels.

prompt: Group similar support tickets to see which problems keep coming up, with no categories set.
why: There are no categories set up front; similar tickets are grouped to see what keeps coming up. That's clustering.
trap: Routing to set queues would be classification.
